intro:
השבוע נתנסה באימון מודל שחוזה אירועים דיכוטומיים (כן / לא) באמצעות רגרסיה לוגיסטית.

נלמד לאמן מודל על חלק אחד של הנתונים, ולהשתמש בו כדי לחזות את התוצאה בחלק אחר שהמודל לא ראה — הרעיון המרכזי של למידת מכונה. נעריך את איכות החיזוי בעזרת confusion matrix, רגישות וסגוליות, ועקומת ROC.

נעבוד עם נתונים אמיתיים של חולי לב.

# Foundations of programming for empirical science
# Week 9
# assignment by < First Name > < Last Name >, id < 123456789 >


#### DATA PREPARATION ####

# 1. Load the data and explore it
df = read.csv("heart.csv")

head(df)
str(df)
summary(df)
table(df$target)

# 2. Binary variable: 1 if blood sugar >= 120, 0 otherwise
df$bs_high = ifelse(df$bs >= 120, 1, 0)

# 3. Split into training (70%) and test (30%)
set.seed(123)
n           = nrow(df)
train_index = sample(1:n, size = round(0.7 * n))

df_training = df[train_index, ]
df_test     = df[-train_index, ]

# 4. Number and percent of observations in each data frame
cat("Training:", nrow(df_training), "rows,", round(nrow(df_training) / n * 100, 1), "%\n")
cat("Test:", nrow(df_test), "rows,", round(nrow(df_test) / n * 100, 1), "%\n")


#### MODEL FITTING ####

# 1. Logistic regression: heart event predicted by the other variables
model = glm(target ~ age + sex + restbps + chol + bs_high + maxhr,
            data = df_training, family = binomial)

# 2. Bonus: print the regression coefficients
summary(model)


#### MODEL EVALUATION ####

# 1. Predicted probabilities for the test set
df_test$pred_prob = predict(model, newdata = df_test, type = "response")

# 2. Predicted class by a 0.5 threshold (1 = high risk)
df_test$pred_class = ifelse(df_test$pred_prob >= 0.5, 1, 0)

# 3. Confusion matrix
cm = table(Actual = df_test$target, Predicted = df_test$pred_class)
print(cm)


#### BONUS ####

library(pROC)

# 1. AUC, sensitivity (accuracy for the sick) and specificity (accuracy for the healthy)
roc_obj = roc(df_test$target, df_test$pred_prob)
auc(roc_obj)

sensitivity = cm["1", "1"] / sum(cm["1", ])
specificity = cm["0", "0"] / sum(cm["0", ])
sensitivity
specificity

# 2. ROC curve for the test set
plot(1 - roc_obj$specificities, roc_obj$sensitivities, type = "l",
     main = "ROC curve - test set",
     xlab = "False Positive Rate", ylab = "True Positive Rate")
abline(0, 1, lty = 2)

# Foundations of programming for empirical science
# Week 9
# assignment by < First Name > < Last Name >, id < 123456789 >

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.metrics import confusion_matrix, roc_curve, roc_auc_score


#### DATA PREPARATION ####

# 1. Load the data and explore it
df = pd.read_csv("heart.csv")

print(df.head())
print(df.info())
print(df.describe())
print(df["target"].value_counts())

# 2. Binary variable: 1 if blood sugar >= 120, 0 otherwise
df["bs_high"] = np.where(df["bs"] >= 120, 1, 0)

# 3. Split into training (70%) and test (30%)
df_training, df_test = train_test_split(df, test_size=0.3, random_state=42)

# 4. Number and percent of observations in each data frame
print("Training:", len(df_training), "rows,", round(len(df_training) / len(df) * 100, 1), "%")
print("Test:", len(df_test), "rows,", round(len(df_test) / len(df) * 100, 1), "%")


#### MODEL FITTING ####

# 1. Logistic regression: heart event predicted by the other variables
predictors = ["age", "sex", "restbps", "chol", "bs_high", "maxhr"]
model = LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000)
model.fit(df_training[predictors], df_training["target"])

# 2. Bonus: print the regression coefficients
print("Intercept:", model.intercept_)
print(pd.Series(model.coef_[0], index=predictors))


#### MODEL EVALUATION ####

# 1. Predicted probabilities for the test set
pred_prob = model.predict_proba(df_test[predictors])[:, 1]

# 2. Predicted class by a 0.5 threshold (1 = high risk)
pred_class = np.where(pred_prob >= 0.5, 1, 0)

# 3. Confusion matrix (rows = actual 0/1, columns = predicted 0/1)
cm = confusion_matrix(df_test["target"], pred_class)
print(cm)


#### BONUS ####

# 1. AUC, sensitivity (accuracy for the sick) and specificity (accuracy for the healthy)
print("AUC:", roc_auc_score(df_test["target"], pred_prob))

tn, fp, fn, tp = cm.ravel()
print("Sensitivity:", tp / (tp + fn))
print("Specificity:", tn / (tn + fp))

# 2. ROC curve for the test set
fpr, tpr, thresholds = roc_curve(df_test["target"], pred_prob)
plt.plot(fpr, tpr)
plt.plot([0, 1], [0, 1], linestyle="--")
plt.title("ROC curve - test set")
plt.xlabel("False Positive Rate")
plt.ylabel("True Positive Rate")
plt.show()
